title: FinServ engagement - model variant & quantization lab notes
content:
Context:
This notebook captures a hands-on lab run during the FinServ pilot (customer: mid-market payments platform). Objective: identify the smallest model+quantization config that meets accuracy and provenance requirements for regulatory QA while keeping 95th P99 latency under 800ms for short-chat flows (avg token length ~120). Upstream system: document ingestion -> dense retrieval (FAISS) -> reranker -> generator with tool-calls for numeric checks.

Constraints & acceptance criteria:
- Accuracy: extraction F1 on numeric fields (amount, date) >= 0.92 on held-out labeled sample of 450 examples.
- Hallucination: Citations required for statements about transactions (>= 90% of responses with at least one provenance link).
- Latency: P95 end-to-end (retrieval + generation) < 800ms for interactive route; P99 generation-only < 600ms.
- Cost: target 40% lower per-token cost vs baseline (baseline = Llama-2-13B FP16 on dedicated GPU).

Experiment summary (high level):
We evaluated 5 model variants across quantization strategies. Measurements captured on a single 80GB A100 instance with Redwood runtime (continuous batching disabled for latency tests). Retrieval latency small (<40ms) with pre-warmed FAISS + cached top-10. Generation stats are median of 50 runs per config.

Observed results (abridged):
Model | Quant | Avg gen latency (ms) | Throughput tok/s | P99 gen latency (ms) | Numeric F1 | Provenance rate
- Llama-2-13B | FP16 | 320 | 210 | 520 | 0.95 | 0.93
- Llama-2-13B | q4_0 (bnb) | 190 | 360 | 400 | 0.93 | 0.91
- Mistral-7B-v0 | q4_0 | 145 | 460 | 290 | 0.88 | 0.86
- Falcon-7B-Instruct | q4_0 | 170 | 420 | 330 | 0.86 | 0.85
- Llama-2-70B | int8/PTQ | 820 | 90 | 1400 | 0.97 | 0.96

Notes on results:
- Llama-2-13B q4_0 produced the best balance: ~40% latency improvement vs FP16 with only a small drop in numeric F1 (0.95 -> 0.93). Provenance behavior stayed acceptable.
- Mistral-7B q4_0 is attractive for cost/latency but failed edge numeric extraction cases (dates and ledger rounding) causing the F1 drop below target.
- 70B high-accuracy model meets accuracy but violates latency and cost SLOs; suggested as a fallback for batch/regulatory audits only.

Quantization observations and gotchas:
- BitsAndBytes q4_0: consistent low-latency wins. However, observed occasional tokenization artifacts for long numeric sequences (e.g., 10,000+ values in a bank statement line) leading to mis-parsing. Mitigation: apply pre-token normalization and a small numeric canonicalization step in preprocessor.
- PTQ/INT8 on 70B: good accuracy but P99 spikes when KV cache misses happen during long conversations; recommend using for asynchronous workflows only.
- QLoRA-style adapters: promising for continuing training on labeled finserv examples (50–200 samples) to recover quantization losses. For this pilot we tried a lightweight LoRA on top of Llama-2-13B q4_0 (2e6 param updates) — saw +0.02 F1 on numeric extraction with negligible latency impact.

Prompt/pipeline tuning notes (experiments run):
1) System prompt templates: tested two families — rule-first (explicit extraction instructions) vs. example-first (few-shot). Results: rule-first + explicit labeling tokens (+EXTRACT/END) reduced hallucinated numeric assertions by 18% and improved provenance mentioning. Use rule-first for regulated answers.

2) Chunking & retrieval: found that 2.5k token retrieval window with overlap 128 tokens balanced context coverage and retrieval time for monthly statements. For very long statements, add a pre-processor that extracts numeric-heavy lines and index them for direct lookup. This improved numeric recall by ~0.04.

3) Reranker: heavy value — a lightweight cross-encoder reranker (distilBERT) before generation increased provenance accuracy by 12% at the cost of +30ms retrieval latency. Worth it for regulated flows.

4) RAG staging: two-stage generation gave best outcomes: (A) generator with conservative temperature (0.0–0.1) to extract and format facts, (B) secondary generator for conversational followups (higher temp allowed). This kept the factuality part deterministic and easy to test.

5) Tooling for numeric verification: integrated a small verification tool-call that runs deterministic arithmetic and ledger lookups against canonicalized chunks. Any generator assertion that includes a numeric value is required to call this tool. This reduced numeric hallucinations to near-zero in test queries.

Failure modes observed during lab runs:
- Token boundary mis-splits causing dates like 01/02/23 -> ambiguous parsing: resolved with a normalization pass.
- Quantized model producing plausible but incorrect rounding (e.g., $1,000.0 -> $100.0). For mission-critical answers, route to FP16 variant or call verifier tool.
- Long-tail legal language where model rephrased policy; we added citation anchors in system prompt and enforced model to return citation indices matched to retrieved chunks.

Decision recommendations (provisional):
- Default production route (interactive regulated flow): Llama-2-13B q4_0 + LoRA adaptor trained on 200 labeled finserv QA pairs; reranker enabled; numeric verifier tool-call mandatory; rule-first system prompt; retrieval window 2.5k.
- Fallback: if numeric verifier flags mismatch or confidence < 0.6 -> route to Llama-2-13B FP16 on dedicated pool (higher latency but preserves accuracy).
- Archive/batch audit route: Llama-2-70B int8 (or FP16 if available) for nightly regulatory report generation.

Operational runbook snippets:
- Canary: roll q4_0 variant to 5% of traffic for 48 hours with metric checks: numeric-F1, provenance-rate, P95 latency. If numeric-F1 drops >0.015 or provenance-rate < 0.88 -> rollback and capture failure traces.
- Monitoring: add alerts for spike in verifier-tool-calls (>10%) and for mismatch rate where verifier rejects generator values (>0.5% of requests).
- Cost controls: enable smart-routing to move low-risk conversational traffic to Mistral-7B q4_0 (expected cost savings), but only after a secondary regression sweep on a larger sample.

Next experiments (actionable):
- Produce a 500-sample labeled delta set focused on edge numeric formats (international formats, micropayment batches). Use for LoRA fine-tune and as regression set. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2025-02-12.
- Evaluate AWQ (GPTQ variant) vs bnb q4_0 on Llama-2-13B for numeric fidelity. Owner: Samuel. ETA: 2025-02-05.
- Run 7-day canary with 5% traffic and automated A/B evaluation against FP16 baseline capturing live P99 tail behavior. Owner: Avery. ETA: start 2025-02-10.

Decision log (short):
- 2025-01-16: Chose Llama-2-13B as baseline for finserv due to balance of accuracy and deployability.
- 2025-01-20: Decided to prototype q4_0 quantization first (fastest wins for latency/cost).
- 2025-01-28: LoRA experiment recovered most accuracy loss; plan to include lightweight adaptor in next canary.

Open questions and risks:
- Is the numeric verifier considered an acceptable audit artifact by customer compliance? Need legal confirmation. Action: Solutions eng -> Compliance to validate.
- Will long-tail legal/policy rephrasing require a larger fine-tune to avoid subtle regulatory misstatements? Risk: small sample LoRA may not capture policy language.

Appendix: quick prompt templates (examples)
- System prompt (rule-first):
  "You are a regulatory assistant. When asked for facts about transactions, extract explicit numeric values only. Provide a citation index for each factual claim in square brackets, e.g. [doc:12]. If you cannot confidently extract the value, respond: \"I don't see that value in the documents.\" Do not hallucinate."

- Extract instruction (to generator):
  "EXTRACT START
   Query: {user_query}
   Return format: JSON with keys [amount, date, currency, citation_indices]
   EXTRACT END"

Notes-to-self: capture trace-ids for any generator-run where verifier-tool returns mismatch; log input chunks and top-3 retrieval ids. Keep these for legal/regulatory debugging.

End of lab notes.
